note: Vol. I No. 52, the last number of Volume I. The town is on page 2 columns 5-6 — a common-schools meeting with its resolutions and delegates, and the memoir of Mrs. Baxley read at her funeral — and on page 3 column 1. THE SEGMENTER HANDLED THIS ISSUE WORST OF THE FOUR: page 3's columns arrive shredded, with lines of two physical columns alternating and many lines reduced to three or four words, so several advertisements standing whole in 1834-11-12 survive here only as fragments and are not re-claimed from them. No letter list of any post office stands in this issue. AMENDED BY T-0328 on 2026-08-29: D. Weaver's standing advertisement for the building on North Water street stands in this issue and was not claimed. It is c010, and it reads LOT 2 — one of the four printings of five that do.

claims.notes: THE TOWN SENDS THREE DELEGATES TO A STATE CONVENTION ON COMMON SCHOOLS AT VANDALIA, first Friday in December 1834, and appoints a committee to draft a memorial to the Legislature praying a special act to regulate common schools in Chicago. It is the month's most consequential civic proceeding and it is the same men over again: Hamilton, Owen and Temple are delegates here and all three sit on the committee of twenty that met at the Exchange Coffee House on 22 November (1834-11-19 c001). Two clergymen appear who are in no other claim in this corpus, Rev. Mr. Truman and Rev. Mr. Freeman. The segmenter alternates this proceeding line by line with an unrelated column, so the resolutions arrive with every second line broken; each supply is bracketed and the meeting's chairman and secretary, whose names fall in the lost half-lines, are not guessed at.

The memoir itself runs down page 3 column 1 of this issue and is a religious narrative, not a topographical one; nothing further is claimed from it.

claims.normalized: […] Sale or To Let, [THE bui]l[d]ing on Lot 2, in block 1, on North [Water] street. Apply to D. WEAVER. […] 12, 18[uncertain: 81 / 34]. — 50
claims.notes:
THE FIRST OF FIVE PRINTINGS OF D. WEAVER'S ADVERTISEMENT, AND T-0328 FOUND IT BY LOOKING. The ticket knew of two printings, 1834-12-17 and 1834-12-24, and they disagree about the lot number. There are five: this one, 1834-12-03, 1834-12-10, 1834-12-17 and 1834-12-24, the advertisement standing week after week from the last number of Vol. I into the fourth of Vol. II. THIS SETTING READS LOT 2, and the digit stands in an otherwise clean line — 'ling on Lot 2, in block 1, on North'. Four of the five printings read 2 and only 1834-12-17 reads 9; see that claim's own note for the tally and the reasoning. The dateline is NOT recorded as an `ad_copy_date` here, deliberately: this setting and 1834-12-03 both read the copy date as Nov. 12 where 1834-12-24 reads Nov. 19 and 1834-12-17 reads Nov. 13, so the last digit of the date is exactly as unreliable in this column as the lot number was, and it is not this run's question. It is filed as its own ticket rather than decided in passing. What is not in doubt: block 1, North Water street, a building standing on it in the autumn of 1834, offered for sale or to let by D. Weaver.

DECIDED BY T-0350 ON 2026-08-29, AND THIS SETTING IS ONE OF THE FOUR THAT CARRY IT. The note above says the day “is not this run's question” and leaves the field empty; the question has now been asked and answered, so the claim gains an `ad_copy_date` of 1834-11-12 with its own verbatim dateline unchanged. This setting is also no longer the earliest printing: two earlier ones were found, 1834-11-12 c015 and 1834-11-19 c012, and the notice ran seven times.

THE COPY DATE IS 12 NOVEMBER 1834, DECIDED BY T-0350 OVER SEVEN PRINTINGS AND BY THE PAPER'S OWN INSERTION KEY. The advertisement ran SEVEN times, not five: it opens in Vol. I No. 50 of 1834-11-12 (c015) and No. 51 of 1834-11-19 (c012), two settings T-0328's tally did not have because neither is findable by the advertiser's name — 1834-11-12 sets it “D. WEAVE.R” and the surviving span of 1834-11-19 prints no name at all. They were found by searching the run for the notice's own body text instead. The datelines across the seven: Nov. 12 at 1834-11-12, 1834-11-19, 1834-11-26 and 1834-12-03; Nov. 13 at 1834-12-17; Nov. 19 at 1834-12-24; and no legible day or month at 1834-12-10. Four to one to one.

AND THE TALLY IS NOT WHAT DECIDES IT — THE ADVERTISEMENT'S OWN KEY DOES. Every legible setting tails its dateline with the figure 50: “1834.—50” at 1834-11-19 and “1881-50” at 1834-11-26, “1831. SO” at 1834-12-03, “1631.—00” at 1834-12-10, “1834-SD” at 1834-12-24 and “1831 -5)” at 1834-11-12. In this paper that trailing figure is not part of the date: it is THE NUMBER OF THE ISSUE THE COPY IS KEYED TO, the first number published on or after the dateline. It is checkable on other advertisers in the same columns — J. Bates's blacksmith-tools notice sets “Nov. 5, 1834.—49” and Vol. I No. 49 was published on 5 November; a For Sale notice sets “Nov. 26, 1834-52” against No. 52 of 26 November; two December notices set “Dec. 16, 1834.-3” and “Dec. 11, 1834.-3” against Vol. II No. 3, the first number published after either date. Vol. I No. 50 was published on 12 NOVEMBER 1834, so a key of 50 admits only a dateline falling after 5 November and on or before 12 November. Nov. 13 and Nov. 19 both fall outside it and would key 51; Nov. 12 is the only one of the three readings the key allows, and it is the reading four of the seven settings print.

THE KEY IS A FUNCTION OF THE DATELINE, NOT A CLAIM ABOUT FIRST APPEARANCE, and that distinction is kept because one of the four control notices breaks the looser version: Bates's “Nov. 5, 1834.—49” does not itself stand in No. 49 of 5 November, but first appears in No. 50. The key records the week the copy was handed in. For this notice the two coincide anyway — it is absent from No. 49 of 1834-11-05 and from No. 48 of 1834-10-29 (checked; the “For Sale or Rent” standing in both is G. Blanshard's, a different notice), and it first stands in No. 50.

THE TICKET'S DOUBT IS ANSWERED RATHER THAN OVERRIDDEN. T-0350 weighed 12 against 19 partly on the ground that Nov. 12 would be a fortnight before the notice's first appearance where Nov. 19 would be a week. Both halves rested on 1834-11-26 being the first appearance; it is the third. Dated 12 November the notice is dated the day it first ran, which is the same-day pattern “Nov. 5, 1834.—49” and “Nov. 26, 1834-52” show.

NOTHING IS AMENDED TO AGREE WITH ANYTHING. Every printing keeps its own verbatim dateline, including the two that read 13 and 19, and each claim's `ad_copy_date.verbatim` is that setting's own text. The dossier is docs/RESEARCH/weaver_building_north_water_block_1.md.
